title: $E_X$ is $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ with $\ell$ inverted
statement:
Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite and $X$ a scheme. Let $\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]$ denote the colimit,
in sheaves of $\cO_{E,X}$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, of
$$
\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cO_{E,X}\xrightarrow{\ \ell\ }\cdots,
$$
with its ring structure as the localization of $\cO_{E,X}$ at $\ell$. Then the map
$\varphi\colon\cO_{E,X}\to E_X$ of [def-sfb-integers-to-subfield], together with the maps
$\ell^{-m}\varphi$ on the $m$-th term, induces an isomorphism of sheaves of rings
$$
\cO_{E,X}[1/\ell]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }E_X .
$$
In particular $\ell$ acts invertibly on $E_X$, and $E_X$ is a flat $\cO_{E,X}$-module.

proof.text: Equip the finite intermediate field E with its norm induced from PadicAlgCl and the resulting normed Q_ell-algebra instance. Apply CondensedRing.integralRegularTelescope to obtain the regular integral-module telescope colimit and its specified zeroth leg. Extend its cocone along the supplied module isomorphism to give a colimit with vertex exactly padicSubfieldIntegralModule. The continuous integral coefficients and the published padic coefficient inclusion agree definitionally. This reuses the compact-denominator, sheafification, and inverse-image argument already proved in the library.

Use the proved helper CondensedRing.module_nsmul_isIso in ContinuousConstructibleIntegralImage on the regular E coefficient module, then map its isomorphism through restriction of scalars. Define t to be the inverse of multiplication by ell. Cocone naturality at each successor gives ell times the next leg equal to the preceding leg. Move the scalar to the target, cancel its invertible endomorphism, and induct to prove alpha_m = alpha_0 followed by t^m. The inverse identities follow from IsIso.

For any other colimit with the stated ring structure, forget the unique module-colimit comparison isomorphism. Its composite with each cocone leg is alpha_m. It preserves the unit because its composite with the zeroth leg is the original coefficient ring map. To prove multiplication preservation, use the following elementary telescope hom-ext argument twice, after tensoring on the right and then on the left: additive colimit-preserving functors carry successor-leg scalar relations to scalar relations; postcomposition with the invertible ell endomorphism of E_X cancels, so equality after the zeroth leg implies equality after every leg and hence equality on the colimit. After the two applications, the multiplication identity reduces to multiplicativity of the two zeroth-leg ring maps. Mon.mkIso upgrades the underlying isomorphism and retains its equations on every stage.

Apply the already proved CondensedRing.integralScalarExtension_exact for the induced normed algebra E. The continuous integral coefficient inclusion is definitionally the published padicIntegersToPadicSubfield, so this is precisely the required finite-limit-preservation statement. Its existing proof uses the regular localization telescope, tensor-colimit compatibility and exact filtered colimits, keeping the source flatness argument.

lean.statement: theorem padicIntegers_invertEll (X : Scheme.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ) : ∃ j : padicIntegersRegularModule X ℓ E ⟶ padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E, j.hom = padicIntegersToPadicSubfield X ℓ E ∧ ∃ t : End (padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E), (ℓ • 𝟙 (padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E)) ≫ t = 𝟙 _ ∧ t ≫ (ℓ • 𝟙 (padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E)) = 𝟙 _ ∧ ∃ α : padicIntegersEllSequence X ℓ E ⟶ (Functor.const ℕ).obj (padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E), (∀ m : ℕ, α.app m = j ≫ t ^ m) ∧ Nonempty (IsColimit ({ pt := padicSubfieldIntegralModule X ℓ E, ι := α } : Cocone (padicIntegersEllSequence X ℓ E))) ∧ (∀ (c : Cocone (padicIntegersEllSequence X ℓ E)), IsColimit c → ∀ [MonObj c.pt.X] [IsCommMonObj c.pt.X], IsMonHom (@id (condensedRingObj (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj ℓ E.1) X ⟶ c.pt.X) (c.ι.app 0).hom) → ∃ e : Mon.mk c.pt.X ≅ Mon.mk (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj E.1) X), ∀ m : ℕ, (c.ι.app m).hom ≫ e.hom.hom = (α.app m).hom) ∧ PreservesFiniteLimits (Mod.extendScalars (padicIntegersToPadicSubfield X ℓ E))
lean.note: The theorem gives the specified fraction cocone with vertex the published E_X as a module colimit and gives its canonical ring-isomorphism comparison for every colimit representative with its localization ring structure. The inverse of multiplication by ell is specified by both inverse equations; every cocone leg is j followed by its mth power, with j underlying exactly the recorded inclusion. The three helper abbreviations only specialize existing regular-module, scalar-restriction, and sequence constructors. No coefficient ring is redefined.
